reference_fields: Win Cowgill, Justin Weaver, Tom Hass, Gary Mount, and Evan Milburn
Fruit Notes Volume 80, Number 3, Summer 2015 grower-panel observations on sweet and sour cherry cultivars in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Maryland

locations.name: Cherry Hill Orchards, Lancaster County, Pennsylvania

categories.name: Mid-Atlantic cherry grower observations
categories.description: Fruit Notes reports grower panel observations from Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Maryland cherry farms, including favorites, cracking and freeze concerns, pick-your-own fit, and varieties that were removed or not favored

rows.name: Rainier
rows.description: Fruit Notes records Rainier as a favorite at Weaver's Orchard, Cherry Hill Orchards, and Terhune Orchards. Source notes: Terhune called it the customer favorite for a mostly pick-your-own clientele that strongly preferred yellow-blush cherries, while Milburn described Rainier-family whites as useful for PYO marketing but listed Rainier among varieties no longer planted because of cracking in their climate

rows.name: Benton
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Benton among Weaver's Orchard favorites, but with a question about yield consistency and possible replacement by Ebony Pearl. Source notes: Weaver also listed Benton among varieties with notable freeze concerns in both 2010 and 2012, with less injury in 2010

rows.name: Regina
rows.harvest_time: late blooming and late enough that Terhune considered it hard to keep pickers out before ripeness
rows.description: Fruit Notes gives mixed grower observations for Regina. Source notes: Weaver listed it as a favorite but said yield consistency was a big problem; Cherry Hill listed it among favorites; Terhune said it looked good but did not taste good there and was poorly timed for a small one-day PYO harvest; Milburn called it the best sweet cherry grown on the East Coast because of dark red crunchy fruit, long stems, late bloom, and little cracking, but noted a vigorous hard-to-train tree, need for late-blooming pollinizers such as Gold and Black Gold, and lower productivity than other varieties

rows.name: Kordia
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Attika, normalized here to Kordia, among Weaver's Orchard favorites with a question about yield consistency and possible fallback to Hedelfingen or Skeena. Source notes: Cherry Hill listed Attica among its favorite varieties

rows.name: Sweetheart
rows.harvest_time: very late in Weaver's Orchard observations
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Sweetheart among Weaver's Orchard favorites only under high tunnels because it cracks and is very late. Source notes: Milburn listed Sweetheart among varieties no longer planted, grouping it with West Coast or BC-bred types that were extreme crackers in their climate, though the grower noted some might work in high tunnels

rows.name: Sandra Rose
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Sandra Rose among Weaver's Orchard favorites but flags it as a bad cracker with possible spring-freeze concern. Source notes: Weaver also listed Sandra Rose among varieties with notable freeze concerns in both 2010 and 2012

rows.name: Cavalier
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Cavalier, also called Rynbrandt in the article, among Weaver's Orchard favorites but suggests replacement with Black Pearl or possibly Kiona. Source notes: Milburn listed Cavalier among varieties no longer planted

rows.name: Royalton
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Royalton among Weaver's Orchard favorites but suggests replacement with Burgundy Pearl. Source notes: Milburn listed Royalton among varieties no longer planted

rows.name: Balaton
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Balaton as a tart cherry favorite at Weaver's Orchard. Source notes: the article includes a photo caption for Balaton tart cherry pie, misspelled as Baleton in the caption

rows.name: Montmorency
rows.harvest_time: too late for Milburn's preferred tart-cherry timing; later than Terhune's desired one-weekend PYO harvest
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Montmorency as a tart cherry favorite at Weaver's Orchard and as Terhune's tart cherry. Source notes: Terhune said customers found Montmorency very popular but timing was difficult for their small PYO block, while Milburn said Montmorency was too late compared with Galaxy

rows.name: Erdi Jubileum
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Jubileum as Weaver's personal favorite tart cherry to eat, while noting that it had not yet been proven as a sound winner in that grower's system

rows.name: Hedelfingen
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Hedelfingen as one possible current option while Weaver considered Attika yield consistency, and Cherry Hill listed Hedelfingen among its favorite sweet cherries

rows.name: Skeena
rows.description: Fruit Notes mentions Skeena as a possible current option for Weaver's Orchard while the grower considered Attika yield consistency

rows.name: Vernon
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Vernon among Cherry Hill Orchards' favorite sweet cherry varieties

rows.name: Summit
rows.harvest_time: ripens with Vandalay in Milburn's early to mid-season planting
rows.description: Fruit Notes reports sharply different Summit observations. Source notes: Cherry Hill listed Summit among favorites; Milburn described Summit as huge, dark red, best tasting, highly productive, and with no negatives; Weaver listed Summit among varieties that had not worked there and among varieties with notable freeze concerns in both 2010 and 2012

rows.name: Emperor Francis
rows.harvest_time: after Summit and Vandalay but before Regina in Milburn's listed ripening order
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Emperor Francis among Cherry Hill Orchards' favorites. Source notes: Milburn called it an old standard white cherry and the best choice for that season slot in their new planting

rows.name: NY 32
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Ebony among Cherry Hill Orchards' favorite sweet cherries and mentions Ebony Pearl as a possible replacement for Benton at Weaver's Orchard

rows.name: NY 8139
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Black Pearl among Cherry Hill Orchards' favorites and mentions it as a possible replacement for Cavalier at Weaver's Orchard

rows.name: NY 38L
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Burgundy Pearl among Cherry Hill Orchards' favorites and mentions it as a possible replacement for Royalton at Weaver's Orchard

rows.name: Black York
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Black York among Cherry Hill Orchards' favorite sweet cherry varieties

rows.name: Somerset
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Somerset among Terhune Orchards' favorite sweet cherries. Source notes: Milburn listed Somerset among varieties no longer planted

rows.name: Hartland
rows.harvest_time: first in Milburn's listed ripening order for the 2010 early to mid-season planting
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Hartland among Terhune Orchards' favorites. Source notes: Milburn described Hartland as extremely productive, spreading, and a great pollinizer, while noting it can crack in rainy periods; Weaver listed Hartland among varieties with notable freeze concerns in 2010 and 2012, with less injury in 2012

rows.name: Chelan
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Chelan among Terhune Orchards' favorite sweet cherries. Source notes: Weaver listed Chelan among varieties that had not worked there

rows.name: Schmidt
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Schmidt among Terhune Orchards' favorite sweet cherries. Source notes: Weaver and Cherry Hill both listed Schmidt among varieties that had not worked for them

rows.name: Newfane
rows.harvest_time: after Hartland and before Summit in Milburn's listed ripening order
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes White Gold, normalized here to Newfane, as one of Milburn's six chosen sweet cherry varieties for the 2010 planting. Source notes: Milburn called it a smaller Rainier with great taste, great blush, and value as a pollinizer; Weaver listed White Gold among varieties that had not worked there

rows.name: Vandalay
rows.harvest_time: ripens with Summit in Milburn's early to mid-season planting
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Van-del-lay, normalized here to Vandalay, as one of Milburn's six chosen sweet cherry varieties for the 2010 planting. Source notes: coal black fruit, self fertility, sweet flavor, ripening with Summit, and a tendency to overproduce smaller cherries

rows.name: Galaxy
rows.harvest_time: ripens with mid-season sweet cherries in Milburn's planting
rows.description: Fruit Notes says Galaxy was the only tart cherry planted at Milburn Orchards. Source notes: Milburn reported it ripened with mid-season sweets and was a heavy producer on a semi-dwarfing, spreading tree, while earlier tart varieties had less production and Montmorency was too late

rows.name: Lapins
rows.description: Fruit Notes reports negative grower observations for Lapins. Source notes: Terhune said Regina and Lapins looked good but did not taste good there; Cherry Hill listed Lapins among varieties that had not worked because of decay on self-fruitful varieties and poor flavor; Milburn listed Lapins among varieties no longer planted and grouped West Coast or BC-bred types as extreme crackers in their climate

rows.name: Sam
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Sam among varieties that had not worked at Weaver's Orchard, Cherry Hill Orchards, and Milburn Orchards. Source notes: Cherry Hill grouped its failed self-fruitful varieties with decay and poor flavor concerns

rows.name: Stella
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Stella among Cherry Hill Orchards' varieties that had not worked, with the grower citing decay on self-fruitful varieties and poor flavor as problems

rows.name: Royal Ann
rows.description: Fruit Notes lists Royal Ann, spelled Royal Anne in one source response, among varieties that had not worked at Weaver's Orchard and Cherry Hill Orchards

rows.name: Ridgewood
rows.description: Fruit Notes mentions Black Gold, normalized here to Ridgewood, in two contexts. Source notes: Weaver listed Black Gold among varieties with notable freeze concerns in both 2010 and 2012 and among varieties that had not worked there; Milburn used Black Gold with Gold as a late-blooming pollinizer for Regina
